I apologize if I disturbed the reservation. I thought the table was empty and I didn't notice it was saved. I should’ve asked first, you're right.
It's alright, Rachel. I think it's best to ask if a table is reserved before moving anything. What do you think, Mr Lim? How do you usually prefer to handle these situations?
I think Aisyah's right. It's always better to ask first, especially in crowded places like this.
I usually let others know if a seat is taken, just like with my tissue packet.
Tapping on the table sounds like it could work well. We can all agree to see what others feel before moving in closer. Maybe we can even use a signal before we sit down, like a nod or a wave?
I completely agree, Mr Lim! Regular check-ins can really help us navigate these crowded spaces more smoothly.
I think we could also consider a signal for when someone wants to share a table with someone else, like a thumbs-up from a distance.
I think a thumbs-up signal is a clever idea, Arjun! It keeps things friendly and open without causing interruptions.
Just last week at the hawker centre, someone moved my tissue packet off a reserved seat without checking. It created a bit of a misunderstanding, and I had to explain it was saved.
I think we could set up a simple system like waving or tapping on the table when we need to check if someone's okay with sharing a space.
